summary: Inventoried existing Newton, spatial, history-selection, criterion-factorization and arrangement-dynamics content; no existing translation/covariance certificate matched. Materialized/read Leibniz ThirdPaper1–8 and Clarke ThirdReply1–8 from byte-pinned Newton Project1717 transcriptions; repeated historic archive copies match the selected text. Proved translation-orbit exactness for signed data, metric invariance, the inhabited fixed-point and covariant-selector obstruction, anchored normalization, a nondegenerate two-body control and empty-body control. Corrected two initial proof elaboration errors (metric lemma name and lambda parsing); frozen Challenge unchanged. Sources do not supply the analyst covariance norm; source-based reason/identity premises and both strongest positive replies remain independently open. Rejected unsigned-distance completeness, translation=physicalidentity and PSRalone→relationalism. Exact source locators, boundaries, open candidate and development binding persist in docs/notes/spatial-translation-and-reason.md. Root-premise delta none; final CI remains required. Owner-directed three-criterion analyst comparison 2026-11-09: preserved the original Leibniz/Clarke readings and allowances, with precise unresolved signature, transformation, parameter and identity alternatives in their definition notes. Added explicit framework siblings _4 relational isomorphism, _5 equality of active orbit classes and _6 equality of represented configurations. All comparisons quantify over arbitrary Type carriers and supplied finitary relations/body-permutation subgroup/group action, rather than assuming Euclidean geometry or a finite original spatial domain. Relational isomorphism requires a permitted bijection preserving and reflecting all supplied tuple predicates; quotient equality uses the actual orbit setoid; represented equality is literal carrier equality. Data preservation and orbit completeness yield the two directions between isomorphism and quotient identity; orbit triviality yields represented equality. A bounded typed criterion selector proves joint equivalence by cases with these assumptions. Passive bijective chart transport separately preserves relational, transported quotient and represented criteria. Marker controls separate isomorphism from quotient identity when orbit completeness is omitted, quotient identity from represented identity when orbit triviality is omitted, and quotient identity from relational isomorphism when preservation is omitted; the other relevant assumptions are explicitly retained. A fixed-label marker model witnesses all assumptions together and all criteria reflexively. These finite marker fixtures witness only the stated structural interpretations, not complete physical data, source fidelity, or metaphysical possibility. No new same-configuration primitive, historical attribution or root-premise discharge. Existing bridge plan in the spatial-symmetry-reason-adequacy candidate still needs complete-data/allowed-transformation applicability and independent adequate-reason premises before root-explanation use. Original completion count zero; three new analyst criteria are candidate progress only. Rejected substitutes remain coordinate inequality as absolute-place individuation, translation or unsigned distance equality as full relational sameness, and active relocation as passive chart change. Existing TranslationBoundary.orbit_iff/fixed_iff and WorldIndexedSources.model retain their exact earlier scopes; none supplies the missing original mapping.
